content.text:
Done. Added a dependency-free test harness; compiles clean under `-Xlint:all` and all 7 cases pass.

The suite covers the behaviors worth pinning down: a normal hit, no-match, the both-ends case, empty array, single element, negatives, and — importantly — the overflow guard. That last test is meaningful: `1 + Integer.MAX_VALUE` wraps to `Integer.MIN_VALUE` under `int` arithmetic, so a `MIN_VALUE` target would false-match; the `long` widening makes the real sum `2147483648` ≠ `MIN_VALUE`, so it correctly returns `false`. If someone reverts the `long` fix, that test goes red.

Two honest notes:
- My first edit was sloppy (placeholder counters, a nonsensical overflow test, dead `cases` array). I caught and rewrote it rather than leaving it — but I should have written it cleanly the first time.
- This is genuinely the last additive thing I had in mind. The harness is the value-add I committed to; beyond it, further "refactoring" of these now ~80 lines would be churn. If you want a different direction (return indices, handle unsorted input, split into files, real JUnit), name it and I'll do that specific thing.
